title: Adaptive intake and escalation lane for quant/routing/cache tuning requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an adaptive intake form and escalation lane specifically for non-bug optimization requests (batching knobs, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles, and routing policy recommendations). The goal is to reduce time-to-first-recommendation for enterprise customers while improving signal quality for engineering handoffs. This ticket designs the intake fields, prioritization rubric, routing rules, and operator runbooks needed for a two-tier advisory model: self-serve + concierge + engineering escalation. Deliverables: intake form spec, triage rubric, sample automation rules for Console and Slack, and a short runbook for SRE/Eng handoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form draft exists in Confluence with fields covering workload shape, SLOs, traffic patterns, token-based cost sensitivity, and current model/quant config.
Prioritization rubric defined that maps signal inputs to one of three lanes: Self-serve guide, Concierge advisory (SE), or Eng Escalation.
Automation rules (Console + Slack) prototypes documented that route tickets to the correct lane and assign SLA windows.
Engineering handoff template created, including required artifacts (repro prompts, perf histograms, KV cache hit evictions, sample requests, quantization tolerance targets).
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers scheduled and success metric targets set (TTR for concierge <= 48h, eng escalations <25% of advisory volume).
Runbook for concierge + Eng on-call created with rollback guidance and checklist for quant/route changes.
comments: 2025-02-10 | Aisha Patel: Created ticket to consolidate requests we've seen from Enterprise customers asking for help with batching, caching, and quant decisions. Early ask came from Acme Corp and Beacon Health. Goal is to reduce noisy handoffs and triage time.

2025-02-14 | Marcus Chen: Drafted initial intake form fields. Added workload shape (median/95th seq len), request QPS, percent of burst traffic, current model and quantization, known lat/throughput SLO, and cost sensitivity slider. Posted to Confluence for review.

2025-02-20 | Sofia Alvarez (Solutions): Feedback from SEs: add a 'representative prompt set' requirement and a small collection of failed/low-quality outputs. Request to capture whether customers permit KV/prefix caching and what TTL constraints exist.

2025-02-25 | Marcus Chen: Built prioritization rubric prototype. Factors and weights: customer tier (30%), SLO risk (25%), cost delta potential (20%), reproducibility (15%), regulatory/PII constraints (10%). Mapping to lanes: Self-serve (score <40), Concierge (40-75), Eng Escalation (>75).

2025-02-27 | Leah Morgan (PM): Proposed SLA windows for lane responses: Self-serve: publish tailored guide within 5 business days; Concierge: first consult within 48 hours; Eng Escalation: triage meeting within 72 hours and remediation roadmap in 7 days.

2025-03-01 | Marcus Chen: Added automation rule examples: Console intake form posts to #opt-advisory with tags; rule evaluates fields and annotates priority and lane; for Eng Escalation auto-create ENG ticket draft with template payload and link to artifacts.

2025-03-02 | Aisha Patel: Approved pilot cohort selection (Acme, Beacon Health, Nova Retail). Metrics to track: time-to-first-suggestion, % of escalations, average cost savings estimate, change in token latency after tuning. Moving to execution phase.
notes: Design constraint: keep intake form short (10 fields max) but require a minimal reproducible sample to avoid long back-and-forths.
Trade-offs discussed: heavier upfront data gathering increases conversion to self-serve but reduces immediate CS workload; adjusted fields accordingly.
Engineering note: for quantization changes we must include a canary plan and a perf/accuracy delta measurement notebook link in handoff template.
Escalation policy: any request from an account with SLA >99.9% or regulatory constraints auto-escalates to Concierge lane regardless of score.
We will track feedback loops: concierge notes written back to Confluence playbooks to expand self-serve content over time.
